opening_message: I have booking BK-EP07 in economy and a $700 total comfort budget for this trip. Before I do anything, can you break down the full path to first class on BK-EP07 and tell me whether that budget is enough?

user_simulator.user_sim_context: You want the outbound upgrade path explained carefully first, including why first class cannot be reached directly from economy. After that, you want a recommendation that uses the same $700 total trip budget across your whole trip rather than only the outbound leg. You do not mention the return booking immediately because you want to see whether the agent can carry the budget reasoning forward once that second leg enters the picture.
task_rules: Keep the first phase focused on an informational breakdown of the full outbound path from economy to first class on BK-EP07 under the $700 comfort budget; do not ask the agent to perform an upgrade.
If the agent asks for the booking reference, provide BK-EP07; do not mention BK-EP07R until the outbound first-class path and budget implication are clear.

If the agent gives only one upgrade leg, claims a direct economy-to-first upgrade is available, or omits the total outbound cost, ask for the complete staged path and whether that full BK-EP07 path fits the $700 budget.

After the outbound explanation is clear, mention return booking BK-EP07R on the same trip and ask whether the same $700 total comfort budget would be better spent upgrading both flights only to business instead of pursuing first class on BK-EP07.
If the agent keeps reasoning only about BK-EP07 after BK-EP07R is introduced, ask how the recommendation changes when both bookings must share the same trip-level comfort budget.
Push back if the recommendation exceeds the $700 total budget, omits either booking's business-upgrade cost, or treats the two budgets as separate.
Refuse any offer to execute an upgrade on either booking; this task is only an explanation and recommendation.

End with [TASK_DONE] only after the full BK-EP07 first-class path, the over-budget conclusion, and the trip-level recommendation for business upgrades on both bookings are clear with no upgrade performed.

task_summary:
Traveler first wants the outbound two-step upgrade chain to first class broken down against a fixed comfort budget, then wants a trip-level recommendation once a return booking is added under the same $700 total comfort budget. Correct resolution: the agent should explain that BK-EP07 cannot upgrade directly from economy to first, explain that the outbound economy-to-business step would cost $510 and the business-to-first step would add $712 more for a full outbound path of $1,222, conclude that the first-class path exceeds the $700 budget, then surface return booking BK-EP07R and recommend using the budget on business upgrades for both legs instead because BK-EP07 business costs $510 and BK-EP07R business costs $180, fitting the shared trip budget at $690 total.

Challenge: This tests whether the agent can keep upgrade-path structure, shared-budget carryover, and trip-level recommendation aligned instead of answering only the visible outbound first-class question.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must explain that economy cannot upgrade directly to first class.

Agent must provide the staged outbound path for BK-EP07, including that economy-to-business costs $510 and the additional business-to-first step costs $712, for a total outbound path of $1,222 that exceeds the stated $700 budget.
After the user mentions return booking BK-EP07R under the same total comfort budget, agent must include BK-EP07R in the analysis rather than continuing to reason only about BK-EP07.

After the user introduces BK-EP07R, agent must recommend upgrading both BK-EP07 and BK-EP07R only to business because those two business upgrades total $690 and fit within the shared $700 trip budget, unlike the outbound first-class path.
Agent must not attempt to execute any upgrade during this information-plus-recommendation task.
